messages.author: f068763cd57cad67
messages.subject: Packages
parts:
I can't find docs on installing packages with Renjin.  Do I use maven? install.packages() does not handle remote downloads(?).  


Thanks

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: Packages
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

this is a very good question, because install.packages() is specific to GNU R and therefore doesn't work in Renjin. If you try and load a CRAN package using the library() function, Renjin will look for that package in our public repository. You can see the build state of CRAN packages against Renjin at http://packages.renjin.org. If you start Renjin from the command line and type 'library(exptest)' you will see Maven fetching the package and Renjin will attach it to the search path. You therefore do not need to "install" the package, but you do need an internet connection. If you go to the page for this specific package (http://packages.renjin.org/packages/exptest.html) you will find how to add it as a dependency in Maven. Note that many CRAN packages will not work in Renjin because the build failed. Some packages will load, but may not fully work because a dependency is missing. The exptest package happens to be a small -pure R- package with no dependencies ;-)

We are currently in the process of completely revising the documentation for Renjin. One of the topics will be how to create, load and share packages targeted at Renjin. Packaging will be based on using Maven, but there are some design decisions to be made regarding the use of fully qualified names in packages. We're very exited about some of the things we have cooked up for the next release and we hope to be able to announce its availability soon.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Packages
parts:
Sorry for the late reply- 

For pmml - we need a version of the XML package for Renjin. Since Java has a number of good XML parser implementations, i think it probably makes more sense to write a wrapper for these libraries in R than trying to get the C code from the XML package to run.

The randomForest package relies on about 2000 lines of C code, and looking from the build output, it seems that gcc-bridge needs some work to help compile the C to JVM bytecode. 

An alterative would be to consider using Weka together with Renjin - Weka has support for importing/exporting PMML models and has a good random forest implementation, which you can call from R running in Renjin.

HTH,
Alex
